### problem set 3 (axioms and models)


1. **Axioms for propositional logic**

   Consider the axiom system that results from our official system when $\textsf{A3}$ is replaced with the axiom:

   $$
   (\neg p \to \neg q) \to (q \to p) \tag{$\textsf{A3}^\ast$}
   $$

   We write $\Gamma \vdash^\ast \varphi$ to indicate that $\varphi$ is derivable from $\Gamma$ in the new system. Now, for all $\Gamma$ and $\varphi$:

   $$
   \Gamma \vdash \varphi \ \Leftrightarrow \ \Gamma \vdash^\ast \varphi.
   $$
   
   Justify the claims below:

   1. For all $\Gamma$ and $\varphi$:

      $$
      \Gamma \vdash \varphi \ \Rightarrow \ \Gamma \vdash^\ast \varphi.
      $$

        Given $\textsf{Proposition 4.3}$, all substition instances of $\textsf{A3}^\ast$ are theorems of our official system. So, if $(\chi_1, \dots, \chi_n)$ is a proof of $\varphi$ from $\Gamma$ in the new system, then we obtain a proof in our system when we replace each occurrence of an instance of $\textsf{A3}^\ast$ in the proof with a proof of the formula in the official system. 
        
   2. The Deduction Theorem for $\vdash^\ast$:

      For all $\Gamma$, $\varphi$, and $\psi$:

      $$
      \Gamma, \varphi \vdash^\ast \psi \ \Leftrightarrow \ \Gamma \vdash^\ast \varphi \to \psi.
      $$
      
      The proof of the Deduction Theorem for $\vdash$ made use only of the fact that all substitution instances of $\textsf{A1}$ and $\textsf{A2}$ are axioms of the system. Since they are all axioms of the new system as well, the proof can be recast as a proof of the Deduction Theorem for $\vdash^\ast$.
      
   3. For all $\varphi$, $\vdash^\ast \varphi \to (\neg \varphi \to \bot)$.
   
   
        From $\textsf{A1}[\neg \varphi/p, \neg \bot/q]$, we obtain:
        $$
          \vdash^\ast \neg \varphi \to (\neg \bot \to   \neg \varphi).
         $$
      $$
       \{\neg \varphi\} \vdash^\ast \neg \bot \to \neg \varphi
        $$
      Given  $\textsf{A3}^\ast[\bot/p, \varphi/q]$, we infer:
      $$
      \{\neg \varphi\} \vdash^\ast \varphi \to \bot
      $$
      $$
      \{\varphi, \neg \varphi\} \vdash^\ast \bot.
      $$
      By the Deduction Theorem for $\vdash^\ast$:
      $$
      \{\varphi \} \vdash^\ast \neg \varphi \to \bot
      $$
      $$
      \vdash^\ast \varphi \to (\neg \varphi \to \bot)
      $$


     
   4. For all $\varphi$, $\vdash^\ast (\neg \varphi \to \varphi) \to \varphi$.
   
      $$
      \{\neg \varphi \to \varphi, \neg \varphi\} \vdash^\ast \varphi
      $$
      $$
      \{\neg \varphi \to \varphi, \neg \varphi\} \vdash^\ast \neg \varphi
      $$
        On the other hand:
        $$
        \vdash^\ast \varphi \to (\neg \varphi \to \bot)
        $$
        Therefore:
        $$
        \{ \neg \varphi \to \varphi, \neg \varphi\} \vdash^\ast \bot
        $$
        $$
        \{ \neg \varphi \to \varphi, \neg \varphi\} \vdash^\ast \neg \top
        $$
        $$
        \{\neg \varphi \to \varphi \} \vdash^\ast \neg \varphi \to \neg \top.
        $$
        Given  $\textsf{A3}^\ast[\varphi/p, \top/q]$, we infer:
        $$
        \{\neg \varphi \to \varphi \} \vdash^\ast  \top \ \to \varphi.
        $$
            Since $\vdash^\ast \top$:
            $$
            \neg \varphi \to \varphi \vdash^\ast \varphi
            $$
            $$
            \vdash^\ast (\neg \varphi \to \varphi) \to \varphi     
            $$



   5. For all $\Gamma$ and $\varphi$:

      $$
      \Gamma \vdash \varphi \ \Rightarrow \ \Gamma \vdash^\ast \varphi.
      $$
          It will suffice to observe that all instances of $\textsf{A3}$ are theorems of the new system. For we should then be able to turn a proof in the official system into a proof in the new system. Given the Deduction Theorem, it suffices to note:
      
      $$
      \{\neg \varphi \to \neg \psi, \neg \varphi \to \psi \} \vdash^\ast \psi \to \varphi
      $$
      
      $$
      \{\neg \varphi \to \neg \psi, \neg \varphi \to \psi\} \vdash^\ast \neg \varphi \to \varphi
      $$
      
      $$
      \{\neg \varphi \to \neg \psi, \neg \varphi \to \psi\} \vdash^\ast  \varphi
      $$
      
       $$
      \{\neg \varphi \to \neg \psi\} \vdash^\ast  (\neg \varphi \to \psi) \to \varphi
      $$
      
      $$
      \vdash^\ast (\neg \varphi \to \neg \psi) \to ((\neg \varphi \to \psi) \to \psi)
      $$
      

2. **Possible worlds models**

   Provide possible worlds models in order to justify that not every substitution instance of the relevant formula is true in every world of the relevant class of models.

   1. $\Diamond p \to \Box p$ / euclidean
   
   2. $\Box (\Box p \to p)$ / symmetric
   
   3. $\Diamond (p \to q) \to (\Diamond p \to \Diamond q)$ / reflexive
   
   4. $\Box \Box p \to \Box p$ / transitive
   
   5. $\Diamond p \to \Box \Diamond p$ / reflexive and transitive
